question.text: The General Anti Avoidance Rules (GAAR), effective in India from April 2017, primarily allow tax authorities to:

answer.text: Tax all AIFs at 35% flat at the fund level.
Re-characterise transactions that lack commercial substance and are entered into mainly for tax avoidance.
Deny SEBI registration to offshore funds.
Impose withholding tax of 20% on all AIF distributions.

explanation.text: The Logic: GAAR empowers tax authorities to look at 'substance over form' and disregard or re-characterise tax-avoidance transactions lacking genuine commercial substance. Complex multi-layered offshore structures that lack economic purpose are the primary targets. The Trap: The flat-35%, SEBI-denial, and 20% withholding options are fabricated provisions. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests GAAR extensively as does Ch 13 Taxation. XIX-E future Cat III also covers GAAR. Manager's Pro-Tip: Post-GAAR+MLI, Mauritius/Singapore feeder structures need demonstrable substance (board in the jurisdiction, local employees, real decision-making) - letter-box structures are high-risk.
